points.point: The Vault's only linkage of signal generators to an AI-related application domain is the high-speed digital/AI-server deck, where signal generators are mapped to RefClk and PLL jitter performance alongside phase noise analyzers.
points.label: contradicted
points.why: says only evidence is OTA integration, not AI-server RefClk/PLL mapping

points.point: The same source maps signal generators to ADC/DAC frontend performance testing, together with spectrum analyzers.
points.label: contradicted
points.why: omits and effectively displaces ADC/DAC frontend mapping

points.point: That instrument mapping comes with no test conditions, and the Vault forbids converting these instrument categories into formal product configurations or capability claims.
points.label: partial
points.why: says no support for identifying most important capabilities, but not no conditions/formal configurations

points.point: The AI context of that high-speed digital source is the Taiwan AI server eco-chain, i.e. AI data-center/server hardware, not AI algorithm testing.
points.label: missing
points.why: no Taiwan AI server/data-center hardware context

points.point: The Vault's AI/ML wireless use case is AI-enhanced CSI feedback using a two-sided AI model to compress and report channel state information — a modem/algorithm topic, not a signal generation capability.
points.label: missing
points.why: no AI-enhanced CSI feedback or two-sided AI model

points.point: In that AI demonstration the test instrument is the R&S CMX500 configured as an AI-enabled base station emulator, not a vector signal generator.
points.label: missing
points.why: does not describe CMX500 as AI-enabled base-station emulator in AI demo

points.point: Where the Vault does list concrete signal generation capabilities (SMW200A: LTE, Cellular IoT, 5G NR R17/18 K171, OFDM K114, custom digital modulation), the stated application is 3GPP NTN component testing, not AI.
points.label: missing
points.why: no SMW200A concrete capabilities or NTN context
